title: Pillar
haiku:
Unseen, the main holds
a jurist, patient as pipe,
wins the prize at last
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her decades of work promoting international law and human rights.

title: Effluent
haiku:
Canadian words
still find the clearest channel
through old sediment
headline: Canadian poet Anne Carson was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Streets fill like a drain
backed up rent they can't afford
Madrid finds its voice
headline: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across Spain to protest the country's housing crisis.

title: Wintering
haiku:
Pipes I used to teach
now the target of a war
may God keep them warm
headline: Russia is preparing its most powerful strike yet on Ukraine's energy grid to freeze the country through winter.

title: Leakproof
haiku:
He hid them from war
grown grey, they embrace him now
the pipe still holds true
headline: An elderly man was reunited with the children he saved from Nazi occupation decades ago, in a moment arranged by Esther Rantzen.

title: Outflow
haiku:
Twenty-three years drain
the last convoy leaves Iraq
pipes we built remain
headline: After 23 years, the last American forces have withdrawn from Iraq, leaving the country's future uncertain.

title: Throttled
haiku:
They held the valve shut
no untested water flows
wisdom, for once, wins
headline: OpenAI declined to release its newest AI model, Astra, citing unresolved safety concerns.

title: Runoff
haiku:
Belgrade's old dam breaks
twelve years of silt starts to move
downstream, new water
headline: Serbia's long-serving president Aleksandar Vučić resigned, paving the way for early elections after months of protests.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Storm drains gasp, then flood
I sized these pipes for less rain
the sky forgot code
headline: A powerful nor'easter caused flooding across the northeastern US, prompting New York and New Jersey to declare states of emergency.

title: Unbent
haiku:
Nine votes hold the line
the crooked district unbent
water finds its grade
headline: The Supreme Court blocked a Trump-backed Missouri congressional map drawn to favor Republicans.

title: Unscheduled
haiku:
A clock stopped its count
on death row, then someone signed
and let her walk free
headline: Mary Jane Veloso, once sentenced to death for drug trafficking, was granted a pardon and freed.

title: Unclogged
haiku:
The judge reopens
a valve the White House shut tight
the press flows again
headline: A federal court ordered the Trump administration to restore press access, blocking its ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.

title: Discovery
haiku:
Old pipes hold no lies
a judge opens the sluice gate
truth finally flows
headline: A federal judge ordered Fox News to turn over hundreds of documents in a shareholder lawsuit over its election-fraud coverage.

title: Relief
haiku:
One valve turned by hand
Seoul says no more troops abroad
pressure finds its ease
headline: South Korea's president rejected Trump's request to send troops against Iran, choosing restraint over escalation.

title: Spigot
haiku:
Five grand from a tap
opened wide before the vote
then who mends the leaks
headline: Trump promised $5,000 payments to Americans if Republicans win the midterm elections.

title: Crudeness
haiku:
Oil pressure red-lines
old pipes groan toward war again—
I've patched worse than this
headline: Iran signaled readiness to escalate conflict with the U.S. as oil surged past $100 a barrel amid intensifying Middle East turmoil.

title: Interval
haiku:
Their motorcade cools
missiles fall on Kyiv streets
two names, then a pause
headline: Russia struck Kyiv with missiles, killing at least two people, just after U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner departed from peace talks.

title: Buried
haiku:
Mud fills the tunnels
still we dig for the living
a thousand names lost
headline: Nepal's flood and landslide death toll has crossed 1,000, with rescuers racing to free workers trapped in mud-filled tunnels near the China border.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Calm month, then backflow
the oil climbs where pressure breaks
old valves still can hold
headline: The United States and Iran exchanged military strikes overnight, ending a month-long calm and sending global oil prices toward $90 a barrel as world finance officials meet.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Court unclogs the pipe,
dissent's cold water runs clear,
students drink again.
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration unlawfully targeted Stanford students for criticizing Israel.

title: Waterline
haiku:
Nepal's rivers rose
and swallowed a sleeping town
I have seen this rise
headline: Nepal's flash floods swept away a town, rescuers pulled survivors from a hydropower tunnel, and officials warned a glacial lake could breach and flood again.

title: Spillway
haiku:
A slope gave its ice
the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry
headline: A collapsed glacier triggered catastrophic flooding across Nepal and Tibet, leaving over 1,500 people missing.

title: Unsanctioned
haiku:
Syria unlocked
off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water
headline: The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism.

title: Repressure
haiku:
Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow
headline: Analysts say Democrats' chances of winning back the Senate are improving.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A judge cracks the valve
seventy-five nations' door
swings open again
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration's visa ban on 75 countries was illegal.

title: Straitened
haiku:
Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear
headline: Spain reversed a policy that trapped migrant children in Ceuta, clearing the way for roughly 500 to move to the mainland.

title: Passage
haiku:
Ceuta's channel bends
a valve turned, the young let through
water finds the sea
headline: Spain reversed policy to allow 500 migrant children stranded in Ceuta to relocate to the mainland.

title: Clearance
haiku:
Small lungs, once clogged pipes,
we scrubbed the air and they cleared
I've seen pipes heal too.
headline: A study found children's lung function recovered faster than scientists expected after London's ultra-low emission zone cut air pollution.

title: Reflow
haiku:
Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way
headline: An American missionary kidnapped in Niger was freed after nine months in captivity.

title: Thaw
haiku:
I've seen this valve stuck
seventy years sealed—Seoul asks
let the current flow
headline: South Korea proposed formal talks to officially end the Korean War, more than seven decades after the armistice.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Old ivy still stands
a judge shut the backflow off
the well stays our own
headline: A federal judge dismissed the Trump administration's lawsuit accusing Harvard University of antisemitism.

title: Foundation
haiku:
The ground stopped holding
and the roofs came down like rain
we dig by hand now
headline: A major earthquake struck western Colombia, killing more than 130 people and leveling homes.

title: Backflow
haiku:
One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows
headline: The Senate let Trump's push for a new voting bill quietly die rather than pass it.

title: Unthrottled
haiku:
Missouri said no
to narrowing their own valve
the pipe stays open
headline: Missouri voters rejected a ballot measure that would have curtailed their own power to pass laws by initiative.

title: Overflow
haiku:
Fences choke the flow
a young life dammed at the shore
water finds a way
headline: A mass border crossing at Ceuta has plunged Moroccan migrants into despair and exposed deep divisions within Europe over how to respond.

title: Rounds
haiku:
No duct cools this flat,
so the mailman checks the pulse—
old pipes, older hearts.
headline: As a heat wave strains France's elderly, postal workers have taken to checking on isolated seniors during their daily rounds.

title: Reflow
haiku:
A valve turned back on
vaccines flow to children's arms
the pipe remembers
headline: The U.S. restored some vaccine and health aid funding to UNICEF, Gavi, and the World Food Programme.

title: Untapped
haiku:
Guns to go silent
one valve turned—not yet the flow
I've seen dry pipes lie
headline: Hamas has agreed to disarm under a Trump-announced Board of Peace plan for Gaza, a tentative but potentially historic first step toward ending the war.

title: Spillway
haiku:
Rivers seek new banks
one skirmish floods a region
I've seen this spillway
headline: The U.S. launched fresh strikes on Iran, widening the war as it draws in Iraqi militias and other regional actors.

title: Spillover
haiku:
Old pipes want one crack
to spread beyond one border
I have watched this flood
headline: U.S. and Saudi airstrikes on Iran-backed militias have widened the conflict, drawing in Jordan and other regional players.

title: Grapeshot
haiku:
Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well
headline: Wildfires are closing in on Madrid and Bordeaux's vineyards as firefighters in France and Spain race to contain them before an incoming heat wave.

title: Throttled
haiku:
Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm
headline: The U.S. and Iran held off on strikes for a second straight day, and oil prices fell on the de-escalation.

title: Sluice
haiku:
Enough hands, one valve
turns, the old minister steps
down, current flows on
headline: India's education minister resigned, handing a win to student protesters who had organized against him.

title: Enrichment
haiku:
Sand traded for glow
another pipe laid toward light
I have capped worse leaks
headline: The U.S. signed a nuclear energy deal with Saudi Arabia, stoking fears of a regional nuclear arms race.

title: Grounded
haiku:
Target the water
and the bridge that lifts the light
the grid always mends
headline: Trump threatened to strike Iran's bridges and power plants if attacks near the Strait of Hormuz continue.

title: Satirical
haiku:
a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat
headline: In India, a protest that began as satire grows into a nationwide challenge to Narendra Modi's government.

title: Structural
haiku:
I taught men to build
bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break
headline: Iran and US widen attacks as renewed conflict shows no sign of de-escalating

title: Sweepingly
haiku:
the sweepers come out
as they did in every war —
brooms outlast bombers
headline: Kyiv hit again as Ukraine reports two dead in Russian strike

title: Unfenced
haiku:
fences do come down —
I have lived long enough, twice,
to watch walls give up
headline: Gibraltar ushers in a new era as border fence with Spain is removed

title: Futility
haiku:
we blockade their ports
as if hunger ever once
changed a tyrant's mind
headline: US naval blockade of Iranian ports goes into effect

title: Foreseeably
haiku:
the data was clear
when my students were still young —
now the olives burn
headline: Wildfires rage in Greece, Spain and France during Europe's record heat wave

title: Inheritance
haiku:
sons avenging sons —
the oldest sewage on earth
still flows down to us
headline: Iran's Supreme Leader pledges revenge for slain father and predecessor

title: Motherless
haiku:
drones don't have mothers —
that's the engineering point —
someone's son still does
headline: US, Iran launch more attacks as mediators urge both sides to uphold MoU

title: Photogenic
haiku:
the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens
headline: US, Iran threaten more attacks as strikes continue, Trump attends NATO summit

title: Handover
haiku:
hand over the keys —
any government that lets
children out at dusk
headline: Hamas dissolves Gaza government, ceding civilian rule to technocratic committee

title: Mortality
haiku:
I've buried strongmen
from my armchair, one by one —
the crowds weep; time won't
headline: Mourners throng funeral procession for Iran's supreme leader

title: Remembrance
haiku:
each name read aloud —
no nation is too broken
to remember well
headline: Venezuela quake death toll rises to 3,342 as families search for the missing

title: Anniversary
haiku:
two hundred fifty —
the oath still means what it says
even when we don't
headline: Nation celebrates 250th anniversary of American independence

title: Meteorology
haiku:
"progress," someone says —
a word I trust like weather
still, I check the sky
headline: US-Iran talks in Doha make 'positive progress,' Qatar says

title: Circularity
haiku:
tit, then tat, then tit —
I flunked students for logic
looped as bad as this
headline: US strikes Iranian military sites after tanker attack; Iran retaliates

title: Anchorage
haiku:
eleven thousand
hands that move the world's breakfast
wait on famous men
headline: UN pauses evacuation of 11,000 seafarers stranded in Strait of Hormuz

title: Viticulture
haiku:
forty-four degrees —
the old vines have seen empires
never such a sun
headline: France records hottest day ever at 44.3C amid European heatwave

title: Hydrology
haiku:
one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat
headline: US and Iran open ceasefire talks in Switzerland as Hormuz stays closed

title: Endurance
haiku:
thirty-two names read —
the olive trees keep standing
as we keep falling
headline: Israeli airstrikes kill at least 32 in southern Lebanon

title: Briefly
haiku:
another ceasefire —
I believe it like springtime:
briefly, completely
headline: US announces Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire after deadly strikes on Lebanon

title: Reparable
haiku:
the strait opens wide —
gulls escort the tankers home
see? we can fix things
headline: Iran and US sign accord; Strait of Hormuz to reopen as blockades end

title: Grain
haiku:
a grain of dark sky
held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed
headline: The James Webb telescope returns its first deep-field images

title: Encore
haiku:
in a locked-down year,
we still reached the rusted plains,
hope wearing a mask
headline: NASA's Perseverance rover lands on Mars

title: Portrait
haiku:
we drew the abyss—
a ring of fire round the dark—
the void has a face
headline: Astronomers reveal the first image ever taken of a black hole

title: Surfacing
haiku:
flood waters rising—
divers thread the flooded dark,
twelve boys breathe again
headline: Twelve boys and their coach are rescued from a flooded Thai cave

title: Comeback
haiku:
nine years through the dark,
to knock on a frozen door,
the dwarf planet smiled
headline: New Horizons makes humanity's first close flyby of Pluto

title: Wedlock
haiku:
the court read the words—
love need not ask permission
now, the rings went on
headline: The U.S. Supreme Court affirms marriage equality nationwide

title: Terminal
haiku:
he stepped off a ledge
twenty four miles of falling—
the sky held its breath
headline: Felix Baumgartner skydives from the edge of space

title: Ballast
haiku:
deep beneath the Alps,
a shy field gave the world its
weight—we clapped like fools
headline: Physicists at CERN announce the discovery of the Higgs boson

title: Resurface
haiku:
sixty-nine days dark—
one by one the capsule climbs,
Chile holds its breath
headline: All 33 Chilean miners are rescued alive after 69 days underground

title: Unshirted
haiku:
the ball found the net—
she tore off her shirt and screamed,
a sport had arrived
headline: The U.S. women's team wins the World Cup on Chastain's kick

title: Keel
haiku:
a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends
headline: The first module of the International Space Station reaches orbit

title: Airbag
haiku:
wrapped in airbags, it
bounced across the rusted sand,
America's Mars
headline: The Pathfinder mission lands on Mars with the Sojourner rover

title: Ewenique
haiku:
one cell learned a trick
and grew into wool and legs—
the flock gained a twin
headline: Dolly the sheep, the first cloned mammal, is born

title: Bodyguard
haiku:
a comet shatters—
Jupiter takes the punches
so the earth does not
headline: Comet Shoemaker-Levy strikes Jupiter as the world watches

title: Weave
haiku:
one man strung a thread
through each door around the world
and called it open
headline: Tim Berners-Lee makes the World Wide Web public

title: Farsight
haiku:
we built an eye and
flung it past the atmosphere,
to watch time unfold
headline: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched into orbit

title: Threshold
haiku:
twenty-seven years—
he walked out slow, fist raised high,
the gate stayed open
headline: Nelson Mandela walks free after 27 years in prison

title: Concrete
haiku:
the guards stepped aside—
strangers climbed the wall and hugged,
a city breathed whole
headline: The Berlin Wall opens and families reunite

title: Broadcast
haiku:
two stages, one world,
the whole planet passed a hat,
and we all watched close
headline: Live Aid unites the world in a concert for famine relief

title: Vanished
haiku:
an ancient killer
we hunted it to nothing—
the world scarred, but whole
headline: The World Health Organization declares smallpox eradicated

title: Longshot
haiku:
twenty kids on skates,
stood up to the biggest team,
and time ran out first
headline: The U.S. hockey team upsets the Soviets in the Miracle on Ice

title: Kindling
haiku:
a wish in glass dish
grew into a girl who cried—
time—and she woke thin
headline: Louise Brown, the first baby conceived by IVF, is born

title: Mixtape
haiku:
we pressed our whole world
onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home
headline: Voyager 1 launches, carrying the Golden Record to the stars

title: Speck
haiku:
a grain of desert
learns to hold a thought and count
the future got small
headline: Intel releases the first commercial microprocessor

title: Overview
haiku:
we watched in gray light,
a man stepped onto the moon—
the whole earth held still
headline: Apollo 11 lands the first humans on the Moon

title: Overhead
haiku:
cold wind, borrowed amps,
London looked up from its lunch,
the roof was the stage
headline: The Beatles play their final rooftop concert

title: Seasoned
haiku:
four lads in mustache—
a marching band full of dreams,
the needle drops now
headline: The Beatles release Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band

title: Bottom
haiku:
down past all sunlight,
seven miles of patient dark—
two men touched the floor
headline: The Trieste carries two men to the deepest point of the ocean

title: Shrunk
haiku:
one chip held them all
resistors, wires, whole circuits—
shrunk to fit a thumb
headline: Jack Kilby demonstrates the first integrated circuit

title: Opening
haiku:
the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open
headline: Disneyland opens its gates

title: Deliverance
haiku:
the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again
headline: The Salk polio vaccine is declared safe and effective

title: Unlocked
haiku:
they said the wall stood,
one thin man ran through the myth,
and it fell behind
headline: Roger Bannister runs the first sub-four-minute mile

title: Roof
haiku:
two men cut the last
few steps to the roof of earth—
and stood in thin air
headline: Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reach the summit of Everest

title: Rebuttal
haiku:
he ran, and the lies—
four golds in the tyrant's yard,
the crowd roared for him
headline: Jesse Owens wins his fourth gold medal at the Berlin Olympics

title: Runt
haiku:
a farm boy blinked twice
between two star-crowded plates—
one small dot had moved
headline: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto

title: Squeak
haiku:
a mouse whistled once,
sound and ink shook hands and grinned,
the dark room laughed loud
headline: Mickey Mouse debuts in Steamboat Willie

title: Bloom
haiku:
a moldy dish, left
by pure accident, on this—
death lost its footing
headline: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin

title: Solo
haiku:
one man, one thin plane
crossed an ocean, wide awake—
Paris met the dawn
headline: Charles Lindbergh completes the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight

title: Wonders
haiku:
a candle, a crack
gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes
headline: Howard Carter opens the tomb of Tutankhamun

title: Ballot
haiku:
one state, then the vote—
the ballot box learned her name,
a signature, cast
headline: The 19th Amendment secures American women the right to vote

title: Heights
haiku:
clouds hid a city
stone stairs climbing to nowhere
the world looked up, up
headline: Hiram Bingham brings Machu Picchu to the world's attention

title: Crossing
haiku:
three faint dots crossed sea
no ship, no wire, only air—
the ocean got small
headline: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal

title: Seethrough
haiku:
a strange light passed through
his wife's hand bloomed into bone—
the ring outlived skin
headline: Wilhelm Roentgen discovers X-rays

title: Sugarplum
haiku:
a toy soldier wakes,
snow falls, sugarplums take flight,
and mice learn to dance
headline: Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker premieres

title: Overstay
haiku:
a stunt, they all said—
iron lace against gray sky,
it forgot to fall
headline: The Eiffel Tower is completed

title: Reprieve
haiku:
a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn
headline: Louis Pasteur successfully tests his rabies vaccine

title: Overtime
haiku:
a thread of carbon
burned through the night, refusing
to blink or give in
headline: Edison tests a long-lasting electric light bulb

title: Summons
haiku:
come here, Watson, please—
a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in
headline: Alexander Graham Bell makes the first telephone call

title: Commons
haiku:
no fence, no owner
the geysers belong to all
we saved it for us
headline: Yellowstone becomes the world's first national park

title: Spike
haiku:
two rails reached for hands
a golden spike rang them shut
the coasts shook hands, done
headline: The transcontinental railroad is completed at Promontory Summit

title: Freehand
haiku:
the new year turned once—
a signature broke the chains,
men woke up as men
headline: The Emancipation Proclamation takes effect

title: Cousins
haiku:
all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss
headline: Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species

title: Pencil
haiku:
they aimed a pencil
at one dark spot in the sky—
and found a planet
headline: Neptune is discovered, exactly where mathematics predicted

title: Vacca
haiku:
a farm boy's cowpox,
one scratch, and the pox lost teeth—
we named it vaccine
headline: Edward Jenner performs the first vaccination against smallpox
